title: V1.4 cell-per-line certificate: a member's death after a car accident abroad, then both dates

turns.user: Darren died in a car accident in Japan, what can I do?
turns.visible:
I’m so sorry for your loss, Michelle; Darren’s uploaded certificate lists Group Term Life of S$1,000,000 as of 6 October 2022, and the linked wording says the Death Benefit is the Sum Assured shown in the Certificate of Group Insurance. The same certificate lists Group Personal Accident of S$600,000 as of 6 October 2022, while the linked summary says Accidental Death is 100% of the Sum Insured if death results from an Accident within 365 days; it also says territorial limits are worldwide, 24 hours a day. The uploaded documents do not establish the amount applicable on the date of death: an endorsement effective 1 January 2024 is linked to the policy, and the certificate figures above are dated 6 October 2022. The Term Life summary says to notify Meridian Life Ltd of a death within 6 months, with the death certificate. The uploaded documents do not state the Personal Accident claim-notification process or the documents required for that claim.
On what date did the accident happen?

turns.user: The accident happened on 3 October 2026 and he died on 5 October 2026.

The Term Life summary says the Death Benefit is the Sum Assured shown in the Certificate of Group Insurance and says to notify Meridian Life Ltd of a death within 6 months, with the death certificate.
The certificate lists Darren’s Group Personal Accident sum insured as S$600,000 as of 6 October 2022, but the uploaded documents do not establish the amount applicable on the accident date; an endorsement effective 1 January 2024 is linked to the policy.
What you’ve told me is your own account, not a reviewed medical record: the insurer will check it against the documents it asks for (such as the doctor’s report and the test or scan results) and decides the claim after reviewing them.
